_comment: Cycle of Prayer corpus schema v1.4. Records the rotation of prayer subjects that a diocese, parish, or the worldwide Anglican Communion itself publishes for use in the Prayers of the People/intercessions. Six cycleTypes are supported -- see `cycleType` below -- because not every source's cycle is anchored to specific calendar dates: some republish a dated cycle annually ('dated'), some publish a standing monthly-recurring cycle keyed by bare day-of-month with no year ('monthly-recurring'), some publish a standing annual cycle keyed by month+day-of-month with no year, repeating every calendar year including Feb 29 in leap years ('annual-recurring', added 2026-09-29 for Long Island), some publish a standing monthly cycle keyed to the Nth Sunday of each month rather than a fixed day-of-month, with no year ('ordinal-sunday-monthly', added 2026-09-29 for Hawai'i), some publish a standing annual cycle keyed by ISO week-of-year (1-53) rather than a calendar date, repeating every calendar year with no year at all ('week-of-year-recurring', added 2026-09-30 for Mississippi), and some publish a standing 7-entry cycle keyed by day-of-week that repeats every single week with no year at all ('day-of-week-recurring', added 2026-09-30 for Navajoland). Three scopes are supported -- see `scope` below -- for the three tiers this corpus holds: a diocese's own cycle of its parishes ('diocese'), one parish's own cycle of its individual members ('parish'), or the single worldwide Communion-wide cycle of dioceses/provinces ('communion'). Designed to hold cycles from multiple dioceses, parishes, and ecclesial bodies side by side without forcing them into a single body's own conventions.
namingConvention: For a diocese-level file (scope 'diocese', the default): cycleType 'dated' -> <body-slug>-<diocese-slug>-<year>.json, e.g. episcopal-western-oregon-2026.json -- one file per diocese per year, because a diocese republishes its own dated cycle every year and the week-to-subject mapping is not guaranteed stable year over year. cycleType 'monthly-recurring', 'annual-recurring', 'ordinal-sunday-monthly', 'week-of-year-recurring', or 'day-of-week-recurring' -> <body-slug>-<diocese-slug>.json, e.g. episcopal-arkansas.json -- no year suffix for any of the five no-year cycleTypes, since none of them is scoped to any one year and none is expected to need a new file every year the way a dated cycle does. For a parish-level file (scope 'parish'), the parish's own slug is appended: <body-slug>-<diocese-slug>-<parish-slug>.json for a no-year cycleType (e.g. episcopal-western-oregon-st-bede.json), or with a trailing -<year> for 'dated'. For a communion-level file (scope 'communion' -- the single worldwide cycle, not scoped to any one diocese), there is no diocese segment at all: <body-slug>-<year>.json, e.g. anglican-communion-2026.json. All slugs are kebab-case and must match this file's own `body`/`dioceseShort`/`parishShort` fields exactly (checked by scripts/cycles-of-prayer/validate.mjs).

id.note: Matches the filename (without .json). See namingConvention above for the exact pattern per scope/cycleType.

body.note: The ecclesial body/communion, e.g. 'The Episcopal Church', 'Roman Catholic Church', 'Anglican Church in North America', or (for scope 'communion') 'The Anglican Communion' itself. Free text, not a closed list -- this corpus is deliberately cross-body.

bodySlug.note: Kebab-case slug of `body`, e.g. 'episcopal'. Used in the filename.

diocese.note: Full published name of the diocese, exactly as the source document gives it, e.g. 'The Episcopal Church in Western Oregon'. Required for scope 'diocese' or 'parish' (a parish's own cycle still records which diocese it belongs to); ABSENT for scope 'communion', which is not scoped to any one diocese.

dioceseShort.note: Kebab-case slug used in the filename, e.g. 'western-oregon'. Same absence rule as `diocese`.

scope.note: 'diocese' (the default when absent, for every file predating this field's addition): this file is a diocese's own cycle of its parishes/categories, per subjectShape's 'parish'/'category' types. 'parish': this file is instead ONE parish's own internal cycle of its individual members/households -- a different, finer-grained layer beneath the diocese-level cycle (a parish already appears as a single 'parish' subject within its diocese's own file; a scope-'parish' file is that same parish's own list of who IT prays for). Requires `parish`/`parishShort` below. 'communion' (added 2026-09-29): the single worldwide Anglican Cycle of Prayer, rotating through dioceses/provinces across the whole Communion rather than being scoped to one diocese or parish -- per subjectShape's 'diocese'/'province' types. Does NOT use `diocese`/`dioceseShort`/`parish`/`parishShort` at all.

parish.note: Full published name of the parish, exactly as the source gives it, e.g. "St. Bede's Episcopal Church". Absent unless scope is 'parish'.

parishShort.note: Kebab-case slug used in the filename, e.g. 'st-bede'. Absent unless scope is 'parish'.

cycleType.note: 'dated' (the default when this field is absent, for every file predating this field's addition): entries are keyed by a specific ISO calendar date within `year`, per entryShape. 'monthly-recurring': entries are keyed by a bare day-of-month (1-31) that repeats every month with no year at all, per monthlyRecurringEntryShape. 'annual-recurring' (added 2026-09-29): entries are keyed by month+day-of-month (a specific day of a specific month, e.g. 'March 14'), repeating every calendar year with no year at all -- distinct from 'monthly-recurring' in that the SAME day-of-month means something different in each of the 12 months (not one list that repeats 12 times a year), per annualRecurringEntryShape. 'ordinal-sunday-monthly' (added 2026-09-29): entries are keyed by month + which Sunday of that month (1st through 5th), repeating every calendar year with no year at all -- for a source that names 'the 3rd Sunday of March' rather than a fixed calendar date, per ordinalSundayMonthlyEntryShape. 'week-of-year-recurring' (added 2026-09-30 for Mississippi): entries are keyed by a bare ISO 8601 week-of-year number (1-53), one prayer intention held for the WHOLE week, repeating every calendar year with no year at all, per weekOfYearRecurringEntryShape -- distinct from 'monthly-recurring' in that the period that repeats is a calendar year (52/53 slots), not a calendar month (31 slots). 'day-of-week-recurring' (added 2026-09-30 for Navajoland): entries are keyed by day-of-week (Sunday=0 through Saturday=6), one set of prayer subjects per weekday, repeating every single week with no year at all, per dayOfWeekRecurringEntryShape -- the shortest-period recurring cycle in this corpus (7 slots, not 12/31/52). See `year` below for all five no-year types.

year.note: Calendar year this specific cycle covers. A diocese that republishes yearly gets a new file each year, not an update to this one. Must be ABSENT for cycleType 'monthly-recurring', 'annual-recurring', 'ordinal-sunday-monthly', 'week-of-year-recurring', or 'day-of-week-recurring' -- none of the five no-year cycles is scoped to any one year, and the source itself states none; do not invent one.

source.note: Title of the source document exactly as published, e.g. 'Diocesan Cycle of Prayer - 2026'.

sourceFile.note: Filename of the original document this was transcribed from, kept for provenance even though the file itself is not committed.

ingested.note: ISO date this file was built, for provenance.

notes.note: Free-text disclosures about the source -- OCR-adjacent oddities, apparent typos preserved verbatim rather than silently corrected, ambiguous groupings, etc. Empty/absent when there is nothing to disclose.

entries.note: One entry per date (cycleType 'dated'), day-of-month (cycleType 'monthly-recurring'), month+day (cycleType 'annual-recurring'), or month+ordinal-Sunday (cycleType 'ordinal-sunday-monthly') the source names. Ordered exactly as the source orders them (ascending, in every source seen so far).

date.note: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), the date printed in the source for this row. Not computed/derived -- taken directly from the source, which is itself often (but not always) every Sunday of the year.

liturgicalNote.note: The source's own liturgical annotation for this date if it printed one (e.g. 'Palm Sunday', 'Pentecost', '1st Sunday in Lent'). null when the source printed none. This is a disclosed label from the source, not something this app computes or verifies against its own calendar engines -- do not treat it as authoritative for date arithmetic.

subjects.note: One or more prayer subjects for this date. Most dates carry one; some carry several when the source groups multiple parishes (or, occasionally, a whole city's remaining parishes) under a single week. See subjectShape. Order preserved from the source.

day.note: Day-of-month (1-31) as printed in the source, e.g. under the heading 'On the corresponding day of each month, pray for'. Must be unique across the file's entries and strictly ascending. Not every month has a day this high (e.g. day 31 in a 30-day month) -- resolution against a real calendar date is this app's own runtime concern (see js/cycles-of-prayer.js), not something this file encodes.

liturgicalNote.note: Same meaning as entryShape.liturgicalNote, but expected to be null/absent in practice -- a day-of-month recurring cycle is not usually annotated with a liturgical label, since it isn't tied to one calendar date.

month.note: Month (1-12) of this entry, as printed/implied by the source's own calendar grouping.

day.note: Day-of-month (1-31, or 1-29 for February) within `month`, as printed in the source. 29 is valid for February -- a source that includes a Feb 29 entry is naming a genuine leap-day subject, kept as printed; this app's own runtime resolves it only in years that actually have one, never fabricated or dropped here. Entries must be unique by (month, day) and strictly ascending across the whole file (January 1 first, December 31 or the source's own last entry last).

month.note: Month (1-12) of this entry, as printed/implied by the source's own calendar grouping.

ordinal.note: Which Sunday of `month` this entry is for (1 = 1st Sunday, up to 5 for a month with a 5th Sunday), exactly as the source labels it (e.g. '3rd Sunday'). Entries must be unique by (month, ordinal) and strictly ascending within each month, months in calendar order. This app's own runtime (see js/cycles-of-prayer.js) resolves which real calendar Sunday is currently 'in effect' by ordinary calendar arithmetic (which Sunday is the Nth of its month) -- a deterministic computation of WHICH real date an already-disclosed ordinal label refers to, not an invention of new content, and never overrides or corrects the label itself.

liturgicalNote.note: Same meaning as entryShape.liturgicalNote, but expected to be null/absent in practice, same reasoning as monthlyRecurringEntryShape.

week.note: ISO 8601 week-of-year number (1-53) as printed in the source, e.g. under a heading 'Week 14'. Must be unique across the file's entries and strictly ascending. This app's own runtime (see js/cycles-of-prayer.js) resolves which entry is 'in effect' for a given real date by computing that date's own ISO week number and finding the latest entry whose `week` is on or before it, wrapping to the highest-numbered entry for the small handful of dates (the very start of a year, or a rare ISO week 53) that fall before the file's first entry or beyond its last -- a deterministic resolution of an already-disclosed week number, never an invented one.

liturgicalNote.note: Same meaning as entryShape.liturgicalNote, but expected to be null/absent in practice -- a week-of-year recurring cycle is not usually annotated with a liturgical label, since it isn't tied to one calendar date.

subjects.note: Same as entryShape.subjects. The source's own convention for this cycleType is typically ONE subject held for the entire week, not several, but this is not enforced -- transcribe exactly what the source prints.

weekday.note: Day of the week this entry is for, using JavaScript's own Date.getDay() numbering: 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, ... 6 = Saturday. Must be unique across the file's entries. Entries are ordered exactly as the source orders them (typically Sunday through Saturday, i.e. ascending 0-6, but this schema does not require that order beyond 'exactly as printed' per fileShape.entries).

liturgicalNote.note: Same meaning as entryShape.liturgicalNote, but expected to be null/absent in practice -- a day-of-week recurring cycle is not usually annotated with a liturgical label.

type.note: 'parish' is a specific congregation (a parish, mission, or cathedral) -- used in a diocese-level (scope 'diocese') file. 'category' is a named group not tied to one congregation or one family, e.g. 'Diocesan Staff', 'Those in the Ordination Process', a parish's own named ministry ('Brotherhood of St. Andrew'). 'household' is a named individual, couple, or family within ONE parish's own internal cycle (scope 'parish' file only). 'diocese' (scope 'communion' file only, added 2026-09-29): a specific diocese named for that day, alongside the member church/province it belongs to -- see `province` field below. 'province' (scope 'communion' file only): an entire member church/province named for that day with no specific diocese singled out (the worldwide cycle does this on some days, e.g. for a small or non-diocesan jurisdiction).

place.note: The city/town as the source gives it, e.g. 'Portland'. Absent for every other type.

province.note: The member church/province the named diocese belongs to, exactly as the source prints it, e.g. 'The Church in the Province of the West Indies'. Absent for every other type (a type-'province' subject's `name` already IS the province).

name.note: For 'parish': the congregation's own name as printed, e.g. 'St. Alban' or 'Church of the Good Samaritan' (never re-derived or normalized -- see rules). For 'category': the group's full name as printed, e.g. 'Diocesan Staff'. For 'household': the individual/couple/family exactly as printed, including however the source groups spouses, co-listed adults, and children by first name -- never split, re-ordered, or normalized. For 'diocese': the diocese's own name as printed, e.g. 'The Diocese of Belize' (its province goes in the separate `province` field, not appended here). For 'province': the member church/province's own full name as printed, e.g. 'The Anglican Church of Tanzania'.

note.note: Optional free-text disclosure about this specific subject only (e.g. a bilingual/mission congregation sharing a building with another listed parish, or an unexplained typographic marker on a household's name). Absent when there is nothing to note.

rules: Every name is transcribed exactly as the source prints it, including apparent typos (e.g. a stray comma for a period in an abbreviation). This corpus does not silently correct a diocese's own published document -- if something looks like an error, it is preserved as printed and disclosed in the file's own `notes`, never quietly fixed.

A blank date cell in the source's own table means 'same date as the row above' -- it is NOT a separate week. All such rows are folded into the preceding date's `subjects` array, in the order printed, per this schema's grouping rule.

`liturgicalNote` is a disclosed label copied from the source, not a computed value. It must never be used as an input to this app's own liturgical-calendar engines, and this app's own calendar engines must never be used to 'correct' or override it -- the two are deliberately kept apart.

One file per diocese per year for cycleType 'dated'. Do not update a prior year's file in place when a new cycle is published; add a new file with the new year in its id and filename. A 'monthly-recurring' file has no year and is instead updated in place if/when the diocese republishes its standing cycle with different subjects, since there is no per-year identity to preserve.

A diocese/body not yet held in this corpus is added the same way this file's own precedent (episcopal-western-oregon-2026.json) was: transcribe directly from the diocese's own published document, disclose anything ambiguous in `notes`, and validate with scripts/cycles-of-prayer/validate.mjs before committing.

This corpus is deliberately cross-body and cross-tradition (Episcopal, Roman Catholic, or any other body that publishes a cycle of prayer may be added) -- do not assume every file in this directory is Anglican/Episcopal.

Before transcribing a new diocese, check whether its own source is actually date-anchored (weekly/daily, cycleType 'dated') or a standing day-of-month/day-of-week recurring cycle with no year (cycleType 'monthly-recurring') -- do not force one shape into the other (e.g. do not fabricate 12 months of concrete dates to avoid using 'monthly-recurring'). For TEC dioceses specifically, check `tecDioceseRoster` above first -- a recurring cycle that is week-numbered or day-of-week rather than day-of-month does NOT fit 'monthly-recurring' either; raise a genuinely new shape to Josh rather than forcing it in, the same way 'monthly-recurring' itself was added when Arkansas didn't fit 'dated'.

A parish that already appears as a 'parish' subject inside its diocese's own file may ALSO get its own separate scope-'parish' file for its internal household-level cycle -- these are not duplicates or a conflict; one is the diocese praying for the parish (one entry, one week/day), the other is the parish praying for its own members (many entries, one per household). Do not merge them or treat the parish-level file as superseding the diocese-level entry.

A scope-'parish' file's source PDF/document commonly lays members out in a multi-column grid (e.g. 'Day 1' and 'Day 8' printed side by side). A naive copy-pasted text extraction of that layout interleaves the two columns into one run-on line and WILL misassign a name to the wrong day if transcribed as-is -- always transcribe from the source's own rendered page layout (view the actual PDF pages, not a linearized text extraction) to get the grouping right.

There is exactly ONE scope-'communion' file (the worldwide Anglican Cycle of Prayer itself is not diocese- or parish-specific) -- do not create a second one; a new year gets a new file per the usual 'dated' convention, not a second concurrent one. A source covering less than a full year (e.g. only Sept-Dec of a given year) is transcribed as-is with the gap disclosed in `notes`, same as this corpus's existing partial-year diocese files -- never fabricate the missing months.

A scope-'communion' file's source is a multi-column monthly grid, same interleaving risk as a scope-'parish' file (see the rule above) -- transcribe from the rendered page layout, not a linearized text extraction. This was caught concretely 2026-09-29: a linearized extraction of the Anglican Cycle of Prayer silently swapped which diocese belonged to which day within the same week.

Two further no-year cycleTypes were added 2026-09-29, per Josh's direct decision (the same kind of call that added 'monthly-recurring' for Arkansas), when Hawai'i and Long Island's sources turned out to fit neither 'dated' nor 'monthly-recurring': 'annual-recurring' (Long Island -- a full annual cycle keyed by month+day-of-month, different content on every day of the year, repeating every year including a Feb 29 entry for leap years) and 'ordinal-sunday-monthly' (Hawai'i -- keyed by month + which Sunday of that month, e.g. 'the 3rd Sunday of March', with no calendar date printed anywhere in the source at all).

Two more no-year cycleTypes were added 2026-09-30, per Josh's direct decision, for the last two roster-located TEC dioceses that didn't fit any existing shape: 'week-of-year-recurring' (Mississippi -- Josh's own framing: "a different prayer every week for a year"; keyed by ISO week-of-year 1-53, one intention held the whole week, repeating every calendar year) and 'day-of-week-recurring' (Navajoland -- Josh's own framing: "a different prayer daily, repeating every 7 days"; keyed by day-of-week 0-6, repeating every single week, the shortest-period cycle in this corpus). Do not invent a further new cycleType on your own for a future diocese that doesn't fit any of the six -- raise it to Josh the same way all four of these were raised, and see js/cycles-of-prayer.js for how each no-year type's runtime resolution actually works before assuming a new one is needed.
